Hi Anna — great meeting, thanks for the clear list. Looping in our Legal (Tessa) and SE (Vivek / Karthik) so we can provide a consolidated response and the current subprocessors export. High-level answers below while we prepare the attachments you requested:

1) EU region pinning: For customers on our Dedicated and Private plans we support strict region pinning (EU-only) for both storage and inference. For Hosted customers we offer EU-hosted tenancy and routing policies that keep customer traffic in-region as configured, but we do not (by default) provide an absolute contractual guarantee of zero cross-region processing in all failover scenarios.

2) Cross-region processing events: For Hosted customers (our most common model) typical cross-region processing is limited to:
   - Disaster recovery failover (rare, documented, and only after automated health checks fail in primary region)
   - Internal analytics and job scheduling: aggregate telemetry is pseudonymized; raw customer payloads are not used for analytics.
   - Temporary KV cache warmup on standby nodes during autoscale (encrypted in transit, short TTL).

In all cases we encrypt data at rest and in transit, and we offer a Customer Key Management integration so customers can control master keys (bring-your-own-key). For customers requiring a contractual EU-only processing commitment we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment and an explicit addendum in the DPA.

3) Subprocessors: Attached is our current export of subprocessors (includes cloud infra providers, monitoring, and observability vendors). We maintain an opt-out / notification window and a standard audit clause in the DPA for material changes.

Next steps: Tessa will propose DPA redlines focused on transfer language and subprocessors; Vivek will attach a short technical note describing region pinning and failover behavior; I will attach the subprocessors CSV and our standard DPA v3.1 for your procurement team.

Can you confirm whether FinTechCorp will require a legally binding EU-only processing clause, or if a Dedicated deployment + DPA addendum would be sufficient?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Anna — thanks for raising these early. I reviewed FinTechCorp's DPA template and propose the following concise options so procurement can assess legal risk quickly:

Option A — EU-only contractual guarantee (enterprise):
- Applicable if FinTechCorp purchases Dedicated or Private deployment.
- Addendum: Redwood agrees to process FinTechCorp production data only within the EU (list of regions) unless explicit written consent is provided for a specific, temporary cross-region processing event.
- For DR/failover events, require chartered escalation and written approval (or an emergency notification window).

Option B — Hosted with mitigations (standard offering):
- Redwood will route and store data in EU regions based on tenant configuration and implement the following controls: encryption in transit and at rest, customer-managed keys, pseudonymization for telemetry, 30-day notification of subprocessors, contractual subprocessor flowdown.
- For failover, Redwood will document the event and notify FinTechCorp within 72 hours; any cross-region read/write of production payloads is limited to emergency scenarios and logged for audit.

Subprocessors & transfers:
- We can provide a signed annex listing current subprocessors and a commitment to 30-day notice prior to onboarding a new subprocessor that will process production data.
- For EU-only requirement we will include flow-down obligations and limit the set of permitted subprocessors to vendors with EU operations.

Please find attached: Redwood_DPA_v3.1.pdf (redlines visible), subprocessors_list_2025-06-01.csv, and a short technical note (region_pinning_technical_note.pdf) that Vivek prepared describing how pinning is enforced at the routing layer.

If Option A is required, we will need to scope Dedicated capacity and add a short SLA/operational addendum. Happy to set a call with Legal + SE next week to resolve precise language.

Regards,

Hi Marissa / Tessa,

Thanks — that is very helpful and thorough. Procurement is leaning toward Option A given our regulatory requirements; they want a clause that prevents routine cross-border processing for production data and limits any DR exceptions to an explicitly defined process. A few quick follow-ups:

- Can you confirm which subprocessors on your CSV actually handle plaintext production payloads (we only need that subset)?
- For the KMS integration: can we have an option where FinTechCorp manages the customer key so Redwood cannot decrypt without an explicit customer action?
- Can you estimate the monthly cost delta for Dedicated capacity with EU-only pinning for our anticipated baseline (20 qps, 120M tokens/month)?

If you can answer those three items and push a draft addendum for Option A (EU-only processing for Dedicated, DR exception process) we can move to approval. We can also schedule a 30-minute call Thurs to finalize redlines.

Anna
